title: Video Download Failed? Causes and a Five-Minute Checklist | HJ Video Downloader
description: Why downloads break — Unsupported URL, 403, 429, bot checks, missing audio, timeouts — with the fix for each, plus a recommended order of investigation and a quick error-code reference.
h1: Video Download Failed? Start With This Checklist
sub: Work through link, permission, environment, platform — in that order

sections.heading: The order that saves time
paragraphs: Almost every failure falls into one of four buckets: a dirty link, missing access, a missing component in your environment, or a platform-side restriction. Checking them in that order resolves most cases within two steps and avoids the repeated retries that trigger throttling.

sections.heading: Layer 1: the link
paragraphs: The classic symptom is Unsupported URL or an empty result. Confirm you pasted the complete URL from the address bar rather than share text wrapped in hashtags and captions.
The other case is a video that has been deleted, made private or moved behind a membership. Those links are correctly formatted but simply have nothing behind them.

sections.heading: Layer 2: permission and throttling
paragraphs: HTTP 403 and "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" mean the platform wants a session. Drop a Netscape-format cookies file next to app.py (or set COOKIE_FILE) and restart; it is loaded automatically.
HTTP 429 means too many requests. Lower concurrency, pause a few minutes and split big batches into smaller chunks.

sections.heading: Layer 3: your environment
paragraphs: Silent video or unexpectedly low quality usually means ffmpeg is missing, so the streams were never merged. Install it, put it on PATH, retry.
Downloads that stall or time out are typically network jitter or rate limiting on the target side. Raise DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT (default 15 minutes) if the file is genuinely large.

sections.heading: Layer 4: platform limits
paragraphs: Sites occasionally change their signature parameters and everything breaks on the same day. yt-dlp is upgraded automatically at startup, which normally fixes it; set SKIP_YTDLP_UPDATE=1 offline and upgrade by hand.
DRM-protected paid content and live streams that are still running (as opposed to VOD archives) are out of scope.

sections.heading: Error quick reference
paragraphs: Unsupported URL: check the link and whether the site is supported. Video unavailable: content was removed. Private video: author restricted it. HTTP 403: cookies needed or throttled. HTTP 429: too many requests, wait. Login required: configure cookies. Timeout: raise DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT or try off-peak.

conclusion: If all four layers check out, report the exact message with the platform name and a reproducible public link — that is the fastest route to a fix.
